core_protocol_claim: A five-node Besu QBFT authorization system binds CAP2 to chain, contract, resource policy/state and user-key versions, and uses atomic shared Nonce, multi-verifier coordination and fail-closed dependency handling for auditable replay rejection and state-race control.

performance_claims.claim: Per-request live-chain reads account for approximately 98.66%-98.80% of end-to-end latency.
Concurrency is the principal observed end-to-end latency factor.
Fragmentation increases local matching cost, but the end-to-end effect is masked by chain reads.
Hotspot locality raises cache-hit rate without a stable end-to-end latency reduction.
B1 and C1 have a stable engineering-significant cache advantage.
C(P) has a performance or protocol advantage unavailable to Baseline-I.
